options.description: The columns, in the order they are drawn. A string is a column whose heading and `key` are that string. A `State` or a `Computed` of them is followed, which is how an app hides a column, adds one or changes a width: replace the array.
options.name: columns

options.description: The rows. An array is fixed; a `State` or a `Computed` is followed, keeping the cursor and the selection on their keys and rebuilding the rows on screen whose row is a different object than before. Replace the array to change it, and replace a row to change that row.
options.name: rows

options.description: Draw the pointer, the marks and the sort arrow with ASCII only.
options.name: ascii

options.description: The current row, as its key, or the state that holds it: `ListView`'s `current`.
options.name: current

options.description: Whether a row is disabled: drawn muted and passed over, as in a list.
options.name: disabled

options.description: What to show under the heading when there are no rows. Defaults to "Nothing to show".
options.name: empty

options.description: The columns between one column and the next. Defaults to 2, as for `table()`.
options.name: gap

options.description: Whether to draw the heading. Defaults to `true` when any column has one.
options.name: head

options.description: What identifies a row, which the cursor and the selection hold. Defaults to the row itself, which is right for rows that are never replaced; rows fetched again every second -- a process list -- want their own id here, or the cursor loses its row on every update.
options.name: key

options.description: Whether more than one row can be selected, as in a list.
options.name: multiple

options.description: Called with the current row's key and the row on Enter or a double-click.
options.name: onActivate

options.description: The host box's own props: a height, a border, a class.
options.name: props

options.description: Whether to draw a scrollbar. Defaults to `true`.
options.name: scrollbar

options.description: The selected rows, as keys, or the state that holds them: `ListView`'s `selected`.
options.name: selected

options.description: What the rows are sorted by, or the state that holds it: a value is where it starts, a `State` is the state itself, which a click on a heading and a digit write and an app may write. Left out, the rows are in the order they came.
options.name: sort

api.signature: function DataTable<T, K = T>(props: DataTableProps<T, K>): Element

registryDescription: A data table: a list view with a sortable heading, columns fitted to the width, and live rows that keep the selection
